profile.name: Emcure Pharmaceuticals Ltd
profile.founded: 1981, Pune, by Satish Mehta (first-generation entrepreneur); Indian branded generics from 1995
profile.listed: NSE/BSE 10-Jul-2024 (NSE: EMCURE, BSE: 544210). IPO at ₹1,008: fresh issue ₹800.58 cr (78.37 lakh shares + 1.09 lakh employee shares at ₹918) and offer for sale of 1.14 cr shares (₹1,151.45 cr) by promoters and Bain Capital's BC Investments IV
profile.scale: FY26 revenue ₹9,204 cr (US$1 bn+): India 44%, international 56% (Europe 20%, rest of world 20%, Canada 16%)
profile.rankIPM: #13 in the Indian pharmaceutical market by value; #2 in gynaecology (8.3% share); 19 of its top 20 brands rank top-3 in their category (IQVIA MAT Mar-2026)
profile.chronicShare: Chronic ~60%+ of India sales in FY26 (~46% in FY23), reclassifying ARV and gynaecology (company); women's health and cardio-metabolics ~50% of India sales; cardiac 19.1% of sales (#7 in covered market), anti-diabetic 7.9% (#13)
profile.fieldForce: 4,000+ medical representatives (Sep-2026 deck; ~40% of them in Zuventus per the Q4FY26 call); productivity ₹7.0 lakh per rep per month in FY26 vs ₹5.4 lakh in FY24
profile.brands: 10 brand families above ₹100 cr and 32 above ₹50 cr; top brands Orofer XT and Orofer FCM (iron), Tenectase (tenecteplase, 100% share), Metpure-XL, Pause, Bevon, Maxtra, and Sanofi's in-licensed Clexane, Cardace, Lasilactone, Targocid, Amaryl M
profile.complex: ~50% of India revenue and ~30% of international revenue from complex products (iron, chiral molecules, biotherapeutics, injectables, photochemistry)
profile.plants: 13 manufacturing facilities in India (orals, general and oncology injectables, biotech, two API sites at Kurkumbh and Pimpri); approvals incl. USFDA (Sanand injectables, Kadu orals, Kurkumbh/Pimpri API), Health Canada, EDQM, TGA, ANVISA, SAHPRA; 5 R&D centres, 548 scientists
profile.rnd: R&D ₹291 / 287 / 384 cr in FY24-26 (4.4% / 3.6% / 4.2% of revenue); guided 4-5% for FY27

segmentsFy._note: Revenue by geography (₹ cr), company decks

fy26.exceptionalNote: Labour Codes (notified 21-Nov-2025) ₹26.06 cr, legal settlement ₹3.50 cr, consultancy (Canada drug-pricing litigation and the Cutimed deal) ₹1.79 cr (AR FY26 note 37). Screener: −₹30 cr pre-tax, −₹21 cr after tax
fy26.dpsNote: Dividends paid ₹57 cr in FY26 (₹3 a share)

q1fy27.exceptionalNet: +₹24.5 cr: foreign-exchange gain ₹23.0 cr less ₹1.5 cr earn-out fair-value change (Motilal Oswal)
q1fy27.netDebtAug: ~₹1,560 cr after the July Mantra and Gennova payouts; ~₹1,450 cr expected at Sep-26 (CFO)
q1fy27.rowArvShare: ARV ~2/3 of rest of world in Q1; 50-55% for FY27

fy27: Revenue growth 'low to mid-teen'; after Q1, 'more comfortable being at the higher end' (Vikas Thapar, 6-Aug-2026)
EBITDA margin expansion of 70-100bp (Q1FY27 call; 75-100bp in May-2026), assuming no geopolitical upheaval
Gross margin ~59% for FY27 (60-61% at the start of the year) because international is outgrowing India
R&D 4-5% of revenue (3.5% in Q1, to pick up)
India: market-pace growth in Q2FY27 and faster than the market in H2 as Zuventus 'accelerates'; industry growth 8-9%; target low double digits
Net debt ~₹1,450 cr at Sep-26 after the Mantra and Gennova payouts; net cash by end-FY28
Currency assumption ₹92 to the US dollar on average for FY27

deals.sanofi: Exclusive distribution and promotion of Sanofi India's cardiovascular brands (Cardace, Clexane, Targocid, Lasix, Lasilactone) from 13-Mar-2024, initial period five years; Sanofi keeps ownership and manufacturing; Sanofi's field staff on these brands could move to Emcure. Extended in 2025 to oral anti-diabetics Amaryl and Cetapin (billing from Q2FY26). In-licensed products are ~15% of India sales (CEO, May-2026) and grow 'in line with the industry'
deals.novo: Exclusive India distributor of Poviztra (Novo Nordisk's second semaglutide 2.4 mg brand for weight loss), announced 10-Nov-2025; promotion from Dec-2025; price cut in Apr-2026 after generic semaglutide launched (Mar-2026); ~1,000 reps promote it; MASH indication cleared in Jul-2026
deals.roche: Distribution of select Roche nephrology and transplant brands (e.g. CellCept) in India from 1-Apr-2026; no upfront payment; under ₹50 cr a year
deals.zuventus: Bought the 20.42% minority of Zuventus Healthcare (acute-focused India subsidiary, ~40% of the field force) for ₹724.89 cr, completed 3-Oct-2025: ~23x Zuventus' FY26 profit of ₹156.6 cr (revenue ₹1,040.6 cr, down 4%). Founder-CEO Mr Guha left; high field-force attrition in Q4FY26
deals.gennova: Bought the 12.05% minority of Gennova Biopharmaceuticals (biologics; makes Tenectase) from its CEO Dr Sanjay Singh and other individuals for ₹231.87 cr (663,865 shares, ~₹3,493 a share; one or more tranches), announced 14-Jul-2026: implies ~₹1,924 cr for a company with FY26 revenue ₹491.7 cr and profit ₹5.4 cr. Gennova's mRNA vaccine business was divested to Dr Singh. Related-party transaction, stated at arm's length
deals.mantra: Marcan bought Mantra Pharma (Quebec) in Nov-2023 for CAD 94.54 mn plus an earn-out; the sellers chose FY26 performance and were paid CAD 50.23 mn (₹335.77 cr) in Jul-2026, a ₹42.86 cr true-up booked in FY26 (AR note 63)
deals.manx: Tillomed bought products, marketing authorisations and inventory from UK-based Manx Healthcare (asset purchase agreement Apr-2025, ~£19.7 mn per ICICI Direct); 120+ marketing authorisations
deals.cutimed: Mantra bought Cutimed Inc. (Quebec dermatology/cosmetics) on 1-Apr-2026 for up to CAD 5.05 mn (₹33.75 cr)
deals.licences: Voluntary licensee for Gilead's lenacapavir (one of six; DMF filed, registration expected FY27) and, from Jul-2026, MSD's once-monthly oral PrEP candidate (royalty-free, 129 countries); ICMR anti-HPV candidate (Jul-2026)

governance.promoters: 77.83% (Jun-2026; 77.87% at Mar-26): Satish Mehta 39.77%, Everest Trust 7.66% (Sanjay Mehta, trustee), Unity Trust 7.65% (Sunil Mehta, trustee), Samit Mehta 7.14%, Namita Thapar 2.67%, Sanjay Mehta 1.95%, Sunil Mehta 1.50% and others (AR FY26 note 17). No new encumbrance in FY26
governance.mps: Public shareholding is ~22%; the company has said it will raise it to at least 25% under Rule 19(2)(b) of the SCRR (Sep-2024 shareholding filing), i.e. ~2.8% of equity to be sold or issued, which on our reading falls due within three years of listing (Jul-2027); no plan announced by 30-Sep-2026
governance.bain: BC Investments IV (Bain Capital) bought Blackstone's ~13% in Dec-2013/2014 (~₹700 cr); offered up to 72.34 lakh shares in the IPO; held 8.68% at Mar-25 and 3.87% at Mar-26; sold 2.4% (Jul-2025, ~₹563 cr), ~2% (Nov-2025), ~1% (Apr-2026, ₹289 cr), ~2% (Jun-2026, ₹612 cr) and its last 1.02% on 25-Jun-2026 (₹352 cr at ₹1,817): fully exited
governance.pay: Whole-time directors' remuneration ₹54.0 cr in FY26 (Satish Mehta ₹32.4 cr, up from ₹25.6 cr); relatives Vikas Thapar ₹5.2 cr and Sanjay Mehta ₹5.1 cr; ~7% of FY26 profit to owners
governance.relatedParties: Sales to promoter-controlled Avet Lifesciences (the US generics business demerged in 2020) and its Heritage units ₹275.6 cr in FY26 (₹217.3 cr FY25); receivables from them ₹197.1 cr at Mar-26 (Avet alone ₹166.7 cr, ~266 days of its purchases); Avet redeemed ₹250 cr of NCDs held by Emcure in FY25; H.M. Sales Corporation (promoter-linked) earns commission (₹5.2 cr). Avet indemnifies Emcure for the US litigation
governance.usLitigation: US generic drug price-fixing cases (doxycycline etc.) named Heritage, Emcure and Satish Mehta: settlements with the State AGs (final approval 2-Apr-2025), direct purchasers (23-Sep-2024) and end-payers (19-Nov-2025); indirect resellers and opt-out plaintiffs still open; Avet Lifesciences indemnifies Emcure (AR FY26 note 45)
governance.canadaLitigation: Marcan is a defendant in a Canadian generic drug-pricing class action (Eaton v. Teva Canada et al.); a national settlement is in final stages; no estimate
governance.taxSearch: Income-tax search (section 132) in Dec-2020 on Emcure, Zuventus and Gennova; income-tax contingent liabilities ₹100.0 cr at Mar-26 (₹246.9 cr at Mar-25); total contingent liabilities ₹258.9 cr incl. interest
governance.auditors: B S R & Co. LLP (KPMG network)
governance.board: Chairman Berjis Desai (non-executive, retiring at the 2026 AGM); five whole-time directors (Satish Mehta, Samit Mehta, Namita Thapar, Sunil Mehta, Mukund Gurjar); independents Shailesh Ayyangar (ex-Sanofi India MD), Raghu Kumar (ex-Allergan India), Vijay Gokhale (ex-Foreign Secretary), Vidya Yeravdekar, C S Muralidharan (ex-Sun Pharma group CFO, from 1-Apr-2026)

flags: Two EBITDA definitions: the company excludes foreign-exchange gains (₹118.80 cr in FY26) and the earn-out true-up (₹42.86 cr); Screener's annual operating profit includes the true-up and puts exchange gains in other income; Screener's quarterly operating profit includes exchange gains (Q1FY27 ₹532 cr vs company ₹508 cr)
Adjusted PAT (company ₹1,008 cr, +41%) excludes exceptional items, the labour-code charge and the earn-out true-up but keeps ₹118.8 cr of exchange gains (~₹89 cr after tax, ~9% of profit)
Working capital is heavy and rising: inventory + receivables − payables ₹3,153 cr at Mar-26 (34% of revenue); ₹530 cr absorbed in FY26; operating cash flow ₹944 cr = 53% of company EBITDA
Related-party sales to promoter-owned Avet (US) ₹276 cr with ₹197 cr receivable at Mar-26
Purchases of traded goods (in-licensed brands) up 27% to ₹2,397 cr in FY26: 26% of revenue

Minority buyouts at full prices: Zuventus ₹725 cr (~23x profit), Gennova ₹232 cr for 12.05% (implying ~₹1,924 cr for a company that earned ₹5.4 cr in FY26). As purchases of minority stakes they create no goodwill (the premium over book is charged to equity), but they consumed ~₹957 cr of cash in ten months
